title: Sex Discrimination Amendment (Boosting Superannuation for Women) Bill 2014
short_title: Sex Discrimination Amendment (Boosting Superannuation for Women) Bill 2014

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would let companies pay more into the retirement savings of female staff without breaking sex discrimination rules.
It would add a new part to the Sex Discrimination Act 1984 so that employers do not need a special exemption to make these extra payments.
The explanatory memorandum notes that in 2011–12, average superannuation balances were $82,615 for men and $44,866 for women.
changes: Employers could boost superannuation for women employees without violating the Sex Discrimination Act 1984.
The bill would remove the requirement for employers to apply for an exemption under section 44 of the Act to make higher contributions for women.
It would insert a new section into the Act to permit this practice.
summary.affected: Employers and women employees covered by the Sex Discrimination Act 1984.
